The game's own BASIC program, as the freezer found it: the line 10 SYS 2157 ($0801-$080C, tokens 9E '2157'), then the text ' SYSTEM EDITOR<<<E **' at $0810 and, from $0828 to $0866, the tokenised tail of an older BASIC loader (SYS(PEEK(43)+256*PEEK(44)+127) at $084F), then $AA fill at $0868-$086C. Game entry, reached by SYS 2157. Calls the title $0876 (which returns when fire is pressed), falls into the new-game start $0870. Called once; the rest of the game re-enters at $0870.

Treasure pickup for rooms 8 and 9 (room id $100C), called from the pickup dispatcher at $8FA2 for rooms other than 2-7. Room 3 drawing: if flag $1382 is 0, draws the 3x3 keyhole icon ($A763: colour $0C, graphics $AC00) at cell (33,5). Returns A = treasure flag $1373 for draw_room_objects ($BD9B).
Room 5 drawing: if switch flag $1383 is 0, draws the 1x2 switch ($A782) in colour $BD at cell (32,5). Returns A = treasure flag $1376 for draw_room_objects ($BDCF).

Entry inside draw_room6_switch_lock, also called from $8FAF when the room-6 lock opens: fills 3x2 cells of the colour matrix at (19,5) with colour byte $50 through $A67F (colour only, no graphics), then returns A = $1377.

Room 9 drawing: two barriers, the upper one at cell (27,2)/(27,5) in colour $6C (open marks added at (27,3)/(27,6) if flag $1387 is set) and the lower one at (20,13)/(20,16) in colour $9C (marks at (20,14)/(20,17) if $1388 is set). Returns A = treasure flag $137C for draw_room_objects ($BE3D).
Entry inside draw_room9_barriers, called by room9_barriers ($B477) when the lower barrier opens: draws the open marks at cells (20,14) and (20,17), returns A = $137C.

Room id $11 drawing, the fallback of draw_room_objects ($BE5A): if $100C = $11, draws a barrier at cell (10,13)/(10,16) in colour $3C, with the open marks at (10,14)/(10,17) if flag $1389 is set. Any other room: nothing.

Room 2 switch and barrier, called first by the pickup dispatcher ($8E1A); acts only while Mr Hat is in the left part of the screen ($D010 bit 4 clear). Upper floor: at X $AC-$CB the barrier stops him (DEC $D008 each frame) unless flag $1383 (room 5 switch) is set, in which case $1381 = 1 and the barrier is drawn open ($B1D9). Room 3, called by the pickup dispatcher ($8E6C): with Mr Hat in the right part ($D010 bit 4 set) on the upper floor, touching X $0C-$33 (+256) takes the keyhole icon: $1382 = 1, erase_3x3 at cell (33,5). Returns with Z from $1200.

Room 6, called by the pickup dispatcher ($8F24) when zero-page $22 is non-zero; left part, upper floor only. At X $94-$D3, while lock flag $1385 is 0: if the keyhole has been taken ($1382 set) it calls $8FA8 (draws the keyhole icon at (15,5) and the $50 colour patch) and sets $1385; otherwise it pushes Mr Hat back (DEC $D008). Room 8, called from pickup_rooms_8_9 ($B107): left part, upper floor, touching X $5C-$6B takes the switch: $1386 = 1, erase_2x2 at cell (11,5). Returns with Z from $1200.

Room 9 barriers, called from pickup_rooms_8_9 ($B159); left part only. Upper floor, X $DC-$FB: blocked (INC $D008, pushed back to the right) until flag $1384 (room 6 switch) is set, then $1387 = 1 and $8FB3 draws the upper barrier open. Lower floors, X $A4-$C3: blocked (DEC $D008) until $1386 (room 8 switch) is set, then $1388 = 1 and open_room9_lower_barrier ($B29C). Returns with Z from $1200.

Room id $11 barrier, called from check_floor_hazards ($BC9D): left part, lower floors, X $54-$73: blocked (INC $D008) until flag $1380 (room 2 switch) is set, then $1389 = 1 and open_room11_barrier ($B2D0). Returns A = $D010, which the caller tests for bit 4.

Sound effect A, the tail of an IRQ: entered by JMP from $8C2B (and from $89FB), leaves by JMP $EA31 (the KERNAL IRQ end). Counts $1011 up (it is reset to 0 each time, so every call passes), then $B51B silences voice 3 and $B4CE sets volume 15 ($D418), voice 3 triangle with gate ($D412 = $11), attack/decay $20, and a frequency taken from the raster line $D012 (a varying value) for both $D40E and $D40F; then it stores $8BE4 into $D022 (an extra background colour register) and steps $D022 three times. Built on the same pattern as the tune step at $8C41, with fixed operands.

Operand byte (low half of LDA $D012 at $B4E4). All three effects compare it with $C9 and, if higher, would rewrite it and $B4EB/$B4F1 ($61, $01, $91); nothing else writes it and it holds $12, so that rewrite never happens: a leftover of the self-modifying tune pointer of $8C41.
Operand byte (low half of LDA $D012 at $B4EA, the pitch high byte of effect A); target of the never-taken rewrite at $B50E, $B599 and $B62C.
Operand byte (low half of LDA $8BE4 at $B4F0, the value effect A puts into $D022); target of the never-taken rewrite at $B513, $B59E and $B631.
Clears $D40D-$D414 (voice 2 sustain/release and all of voice 3) to 0, then jumps back into effect A at $B4CE to set it going again.

Chooses the IRQ-tail sound, reached from irq_invuln_countdown ($BF5E). If $A877 holds $20 it would play the noise burst $B54B, but $A877 only ever holds $AD or $60, so that test never passes. Otherwise, for room id $100C < 5 goes to $B5B6, for >= 5 to $B5C3; the two are identical.

Sound effect B, IRQ tail: every third call ($1011 counts to 3) silences voice 3 ($B5A6) and restarts it as noise with gate ($D412 = $81), volume 15, attack/decay $20, frequency from the raster line $D012; stores $8BE4 into $D022 and steps it three times; leaves by JMP $EA31. Played while Mr Hat is immune (from $BF47).
Clears $D40D-$D414 (voice 3) and jumps to $B559 to restart the noise burst.

IRQ tail used by sfx_select for rooms below 5 (a second copy at $B5C3 for rooms 5 and up, same code): if the score-tick flag $1015 is 0, goes on to $8C00 (another IRQ stage, which ends at $7C70 or in effect A, $B4C0); if it is set, plays sfx_score_tick ($B5D1).

Sound effect C, the score tick, IRQ tail: steps $D022, counts $1016; after $40 calls ends ($B649 clears $1015 and $1016). Every tenth call ($1011 to $0A) silences voice 3 ($B639) and restarts it as a triangle with gate at the fixed frequency $8888, volume 15, attack/decay $20; stores $8BE4 into $D022 and steps it. $1015 is set by $8AD0, the routine that adds one score step. Leaves by JMP $EA31.
Clears $D40D-$D414 (voice 3) and jumps to $B5EC to retrigger the score tick.
Ends the score tick: $1015 = 0 and $1016 = 0, then JMP $EA31.
Returns A = $DC00 (joystick port 2) when the screen is switched on ($D011 bit 4 set), otherwise A = 0, which matches none of the direction values the callers test. Called from $9357 and $941C.

Reads the sprite-sprite collision register $D01E; if it is exactly $90 (sprites 4 and 7, Mr Hat and the sprite-7 guardian, and no others) calls $4C52 (the kill call, turned into RTS while he is immune). Returns A = a second read of $D01E, which the caller at $4C40 compares with $14 and $18.
Points the IRQ vector $0314/$0315 back at the KERNAL handler $EA31 (with SEI/CLI round it). Called from $7CE8, just before the game sets $1018 = 1 and returns to the title after the last room.

Draws the title screen text and sprites, called from $CDF9 when $1018 = 0. Sprite X high bits off, prints CHR$(31) and CHR$(147) (clear screen), border and background $0C, clears $0400-$07FF ($1744). Copies the screen-code words from $C000 to the screen, each letter twice (code on one row, code+$20 on the row below, the two-row font): MR.HAT (row 10, col 2), OCTOPUS (7 of the 9 letters of OCTOPUSSY, row 12 col 16), SNAILY (row 10 col 30), DYNKY (row 18 col 9), KNIFFY (row 18 col 24), AND ALL OTHERS (row 23 col 12, colour 7), SYSTEMS PRESENTS A NEW GAME WITH (row 2 col 3, colour $0D). The word DOUBLE at $C007 is not drawn. Draws a 3x3-cell object at cell X,Y (X = column, Y = row): colour byte $1C over 3x3 cells and the graphics at $AFF0 ($A67F, $A690), then recolours the two rows below the top (Y+1, Y+2) with $9C. Called from $1087, $668A and $9051 during room set-up.

Guardian step for sprite 3: moves it one pixel left (DEC $D006) and counts $100A; on the fifth count swaps its pointer $07FB between $3B and $3C (the frame the title shows beside OCTOPUS is $3B) and resets $100A; otherwise (and after a swap back to $3B) sets its colour to $0A. Moves Mr Hat across the X high-bit boundary, called from $8919 when $D008 is $00 or $FF: at $00 clears his $D010 bit, puts X at $FE and turns sprite 4 on; at $FF sets the $D010 bit, puts X at $24 (X = $124) and turns sprite 4 off.
JMP from $8900: if sprite 4 is enabled or its X high bit is set, goes on to $8908 (edge check $8912, then hazards and pickups $5590); otherwise returns.
Moves Mr Hat one pixel up (DEC $D009) and sets $D008 = 1. Called from $828F when the stick is up ($DC00 = $7E); the caller moves sprite 5 with him ($D00B).
Moves Mr Hat one pixel down (INC $D009) and sets $D008 = 1. Called from $898A while $D009 < $B4; the caller moves sprite 5 with him.
JMP from $6531: Mr Hat pointer $07FC = $2C (the frame the title shows beside MR.HAT) and Y = $5C, the standing height on the upper floor.
Sets the room id $100C to 6. Called from $607E.

Guardian step for sprite 7, counted by $100D: counts 1-7 show pointer $3D and move it one pixel left (DEC $D00E), counts 8-14 pointer $3E and one pixel right, count 15 resets $100D to 0. $3D is the frame the title shows beside SNAILY. Called from the IRQ at $48B0 and from $B97A.
Sets up sprite 7: pointer $3D, colour 1, Y $B4 (the bottom floor), X $FF, enabled; clears its step counter $100D. Returns A = $D015. Called from $6785.
Runs anim_sprite7_shuffle and returns A = sprite 0 X ($D000). Called from $B99F and $B9A8.
Stores A into $1E08 and sets sprite 3 colour to 6. Called from $809F with A = $FA.
Returns A = $D015 AND $10: non-zero while sprite 4 (Mr Hat) is enabled. Called from $6BF0.
Chooses sprite 0 pointer by height: $3A when $D001 >= $54, else $3F; then anim_sprite7_get_s0x. Returns A = $D000. Called from $684C.
IRQ handler installed at $90F1 (room 4 set-up). If the room id $100C is 7 it runs room7_bounce_sprite3 ($B9C0); otherwise JMP $9300 (room 4 guardians).
Three bytes EE 20 D0 (INC $D020) just before room7_bounce_sprite3; nothing jumps here (the JMP at $B9B7 goes to $B9C0), so it never runs.

Room 7 guardian, sprite 3, bouncing diagonally by self-modified INC/DEC opcodes: X two pixels a frame ($B9C0/$B9C3 become DEC when X >= $FE, INC when X < $60), Y by the pair at $B9C6/$B9C9 (DEC at Y >= $B5, INC below $9C). While Y < $A0 the second Y step is rewritten to INC/DEC $D021 (operand byte $B9CA = $21), so above that line it moves one pixel a frame and steps the background colour instead. Pointer from sprite3_frame_by_y. Ends with JMP $8215 (the next IRQ stage).
Opcode byte of the second X step of room7_bounce_sprite3, rewritten $CE (DEC) or $EE (INC) together with $B9C0.
Opcode byte of the first Y step of room7_bounce_sprite3 (INC/DEC $D007), rewritten with $B9C9.
Opcode byte of the second Y step of room7_bounce_sprite3, rewritten $CE/$EE with $B9C6.

Operand low byte of the second Y step: $07 (acts on $D007, sprite 3 Y) when Y >= $A0, $21 (acts on $D021, the background colour) when Y < $A0. The store at $BA08 is always overwritten by $BA14 or $BA1C.
Clears sprite 3 X high bit (sprite3_clear_xhigh), then sets its pointer $07FB to $3A when Y >= $AC, else $3F. Returns A = sprite 3 X ($D006).
Called from room 4 set-up ($90EA) with A = the wanted $D010: outside room 7 just stores it; in room 7 instead puts sprite 3 at Y $B4 with colour $0B, steps $D022 and clears sprite 3 X high bit.
Clears bit 3 of $D010 (sprite 3 X high bit) and returns A = sprite 3 Y ($D007).
Sets Mr Hat colour $D02B = A (A = $0B from $50F6), sprite 3 Y = $B4, then init_sprite2.

Room guardian step called from the IRQ at $5110: sprite 3 walks left (anim_sprite3_walk_left); sprite 2 moves two pixels a frame between X $70 and $EE, the direction held in the self-modified opcodes at $BA80/$BA83 (DEC from $EE, INC below $70); counts $100A and animates it (anim_sprite2_frame). $100A is shared with the sprite-3 step.
Opcode byte of the first sprite-2 X step (INC/DEC $D004), $EE or $CE; anim_sprite2_frame reads it to know the direction.
Opcode byte of the second sprite-2 X step, rewritten with $BA80.
Sets up sprite 2: Y $5C (upper floor), pointer $24, X high bit off, enabled, colour 1, X $78.

Every fifth count of $100A swaps sprite 2 frames: moving left (opcode $CE at $BA80) between pointers $3D and $3E, moving right between $24 and $29; the store and the reset of $100A are in set_sprite2_pointer.
Stores A into sprite 2 pointer $07FA and clears the frame counter $100A.

Per-room deadly floor spots, called from $5590: first the collision and pickup dispatcher $8E10, then, by room id $100C, kills Mr Hat (JSR $A877 or $55F5, which is JMP $A877) when he stands at an exact height inside an X window ($A97C with A=$01, no stick needed). Heights: $B4 bottom floor, $5C upper floor. Windows: room 4 left X $C8-$EB and right X $18-$33 (+256); room 5 left $24-$53 and $C8-$E7; room 6 left, upper $3C-$5B, lower $34-$5B, $A8-$CB, $DC-$FB; room 7 left $5C-$83; room 9 left $44-$6B; room 8 upper right $04-$33, lower right $24-$4B, lower left $A8-$C7; room $11: room11_barrier, then left upper $B8-$EF. Draws the 2x2-cell treasure gfx_sparkle_ball ($B070) at cell X,Y in colour byte $7C ($A67F colours, $A690 graphics). Called from draw_room_objects for rooms 2 and 4.

Draws the 2x2-cell object gfx_invuln_object ($B0E0) at cell X,Y in colour byte $DC. Called from draw_room_objects for rooms 3 and 7; taking it (the dispatcher at $8E94 and $8F9E) calls $1250, the immunity.
Removes a 2x2-cell object at cell X,Y: colour byte $CC (both nibbles $C) over the cells, drawn with the brick graphics at $AF40. Called after every pickup of a 2x2 object.
Removes a 2x3-cell object (2 wide, 3 high) at cell X,Y the same way as erase_2x2: colour $CC, graphics $AF40. Used for the trophies.
Removes a 3x3-cell object at cell X,Y: colour $CC, graphics $AF40. Used once, for the room 3 keyhole icon (room3_take_keyhole).
Clears the 64 bytes $1371-$13B0: the treasure flags $1371-$137D and the switch, keyhole and barrier flags $1380-$1389, so that every object is back. Called at the start of a game ($6F1C).

Draws the objects of the current room that have not been taken, called from $A4FD just before the screen is switched back on; does nothing while the screen is on ($D011 bit 4 set). By room id $100C: room 2 fixtures ($B1B0), trophy at (14,5) unless $1371, ball at (16,17) unless $1372; room 3 keyhole ($B1EC), invulnerability object at (32,17) unless $1373; room 4 ball at (4,17) unless $1374, ring at (27,17) unless $1375; room 5 switch ($B1FF), yellow trophy at (26,5) unless $1376; room 6 (only if zero-page $22 is non-zero) switch and lock ($B214), yellow trophy at (3,5) unless $1377, green ring at (15,17) unless $1378; room 7 invulnerability object at (16,17) unless $1379; room 8 switch ($B247), ring at (22,6) unless $137A, cyan trophy at (3,16) unless $137B; room 9 barriers ($B25C), green rings at (27,17) unless $137C and (32,17) unless $137D; other rooms draw_room11_barrier.

Draws the trophy at cell X,Y: the 2x2 cup from $B0B0 in the colour byte held in the operand at $BE67 (normally $6C), then the 2x1 foot from $B0D0 at row Y+2 in colour $9C. X,Y are kept in $1E06/$1E07 between the two halves.

Draws the ring at cell X,Y: the top row (gem) from $B090 in the colour byte held at $BEB2 (normally $3C), and the band from $B0A0 at row Y+1 in colour $7C.
Operand of LDA #$3C at $BEB1: the ring gem colour, set to $DC by draw_ring_green for one call.
Draws the trophy with the cup in colour $7C (patches $BE67, calls draw_trophy, restores $6C). Rooms 5 and 6.
Draws the ring with the gem in colour $DC (patches $BEB2, calls draw_ring, restores $3C). Rooms 6 and 9.
Draws the trophy with the cup in colour $3C (patches $BE67, calls draw_trophy, restores $6C). Room 8.

IRQ stage reached from $8215 (JMP): while Mr Hat is immune ($A877 holds RTS, $60, as set by $1250) counts $100F up, steps the sprite multicolours $D025/$D026 each frame (the flashing) and plays sfx_noise_burst; when $100F reaches $FE ends the immunity by writing JSR ($20) back to $4C52 and LDA ($AD) back to $A877 and setting $D026 = $0D, $D025 = $02, then goes on to sfx_select ($B530), as it does when he is not immune. A copy of $1265, which ends at $EA31 instead.
Draws the white mark that shows a barrier open, top half: 2x1 cells at X,Y in colour $1C with the graphics at $AC68 (a drop shape).
Draws the lower white mark of an open barrier: 2x1 cells at X,Y in colour $1C with the graphics at $AC88.

The end screen, drawn instead of the cast by the title set-up $CDC0 when $1018 is non-zero (it is set to 1 at $7CED after the last room): CHR$(31), CHR$(147), border and background $0C, screen cleared ($1744), then WONDERFUL (row 7), YOU HAVE FINISHED YOUR (row 11), MISSION (row 15) from $B7D8-$B7FF in the two-row font (code, and code+$20 on the row below).

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "MR HAT", 6 bytes, copied by $B6A1 to screen $0592 (top) and $05BA (bottom).

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): " DOUBLE ", 8 bytes $C006-$C00D. No reader found (byte search for $C006-$C00D in the whole image, and $B683 skips from $C000 to $C00E): a leftover word the title does not show.
Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "OCTOPUS", 7 bytes, copied by $B6B4 to screen $05F0/$0618.

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "SY " ($13 $19 $00), 3 bytes after OCTOPUS that the copy at $B6B4 (7 bytes) never reaches: the string reads OCTOPUSSY; not shown.
Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "SNAILY", 6 bytes, copied by $B6C7 to screen $05AE/$05D6.

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "DYNKY " (spelt with a Y, as the title screen shows it), 6 bytes, copied by $B6DA to screen $06D9/$0701. The cherries the magazine calls Dinky.
Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "KNIFFY ", 7 bytes, copied by $B6ED to screen $06E8/$0710.

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "AND ALL OTHERS", 14 bytes, copied by $B705 to screen $07A4/$07CC (colour 7, yellow, set at $B718).

Title word, screen codes for the two-cell font at $CE00 (0 = blank, 1-26 = A-Z; the bottom half of each letter is code+32): "SYSTEMS PRESENTS A NEW GAME WITH", 32 bytes $C039-$C058, copied by $B789 to screen $0453 (top) and $047B (bottom), colour 13 set at $B79C.
Unused: 39 zero bytes $C059-$C07F after the title words; no reader found.

Music: end-of-song restart. Reached by JMP from $C119 after the song has ended ($C103). 21 NOPs (room left for patching), then JSR music_init ($C09B) re-arms the player so its next IRQ starts the song again from the first position, and JMP ($CB05) chains to the saved KERNAL IRQ. So the title tune loops for as long as the title is up.

Music: initialise the player. Called by title_setup ($CDC0) and by music_restart ($C095). Clears music_voice_mode ($C437, all three voices play) and music_keys_enabled ($C439, the editor keyboard controls off), then JMPs to music_hook_irq ($C2D8), which saves the current IRQ vector $0314/$0315 in $CB05/$CB06 and points $0314 at music_first_irq ($C2EB). Returns to the caller with interrupts enabled.

Music: called from $C1A3 with Y = music_pattern ($C434): loads that pattern's step length from music_tempo ($C443,Y) into music_tick_count ($C438), then falls through (JMP) to music_set_sid_sound ($C11D), which writes the pattern's SID sound set.

Music: the title IRQ handler ($0314 = $C0AF, set by music_first_irq). Every IRQ it decrements music_tick_count ($C438); until it reaches zero it just chains to the saved KERNAL handler through ($CB05). At zero it reloads the count from music_tempo ($C443,pattern), advances music_step ($C436) and decides: past the end step (music_last_step $CA03) of the pattern's last block (music_block_last $C983) -> next pattern ($C0E4); past step 16 (music_block_len $C43C) of another block -> next block ($C2CD); otherwise play the new step ($C1CC -> $C357). Next pattern: music_pattern ($C434) + 1 while it is within the order entry's last pattern (music_order_last $CADB); otherwise music_position ($C433) + 1 and, while it is within music_song_len ($C43D), start at that entry's first pattern (music_order_first $CAC3, via $C183); otherwise the song has ended ($C103).

Music: the song has ended (or, with the editor keys on, a key other than 1/2/3/F7 was pressed, $C371). SEI, sets CIA 1 timer A latch $DC04/$DC05 to $411B (about 59 IRQs a second on PAL), JSR music_restore_irq ($CB07: $0314 back to the saved KERNAL vector), CLI, JMP music_restart ($C080), which re-arms the player. The SID is not silenced here; the voices ring on until the restart plays its first step.
A single NOP ($EA) between music_song_end's JMP $C080 and music_set_sid_sound: never executed, padding.

Music: write the sound set of pattern X = music_pattern ($C434) into the SID: attack/decay of voices 1-3 from $C543/$C583/$C5C3,X to $D405/$D40C/$D413; sustain/release from $C603/$C643/$C683,X to $D406/$D40D/$D414; pulse width lo from $C6C3/$C703/$C743,X to $D402/$D409/$D410 and hi from $C783/$C7C3/$C803,X to $D403/$D40A/$D411; filter resonance/routing $C843,X to $D417; filter mode/volume $C883,X to $D418; cutoff lo/hi $C8C3/$C903,X to $D415/$D416. The waveforms are applied per note (music_v1_ctrl $C483 and on). So the "instrument" is chosen per pattern, for all three voices at once, not per note.
Music: start order position music_position ($C433): music_pattern ($C434) = music_order_first ($CAC3,position), then falls into music_start_pattern ($C18C).

Music: start pattern Y = music_pattern ($C434). Sets CIA 1 timer A latch $DC04/$DC05 from music_timer_lo/hi ($CA43/$CA83,Y) and force-loads it (ORA #$10 into $DC0E), so each pattern sets its own IRQ rate; JSR $C0A6 (step length and SID sound set); music_block ($C435) = music_block_first ($C943,Y), music_step ($C436) = music_first_step ($C9C3,Y); then computes the block pointer (at $C1B2) and plays the first step.

Music: point $C43A/$C43B at note block music_block ($C435): JSR $C31B (A = block, $C43B = 0), shift left six times (x 64) into $C43B:A, add $CAF2. Block n therefore sits at $CAF2 + 64 x n, with voice 1 at +$11..+$20, voice 2 at +$21..+$30 and voice 3 at +$31..+$40 (steps 1-16). Also entered from music_next_block ($C2D5). Ends with JMP $C357, which plays the current step.

Music, editor keyboard control (only when music_keys_enabled $C439 is non-zero, which the game never sets): A = $C5, the KERNAL's last key. 64 (no key) leaves music_voice_mode ($C437) alone; F7 (3) sets 0, all voices; "1" (56) sets 1, "2" (59) sets 2, "3" (8) sets 3, one voice alone; any other key sets 4, which $C364 treats as stop (music_song_end). Key numbers from the KERNAL matrix (c64-reference). Then JMP $C364.

Music: play step music_step ($C436) of the current block for the three voices, with Z/A = music_voice_mode ($C437) from $C36B. For voice v (1-3) that the mode lets play (mode 0 or v), read the note byte at ($C43A/$C43B) + $10v + step, through $FB/$FC: 0 = nothing (the note holds), $64 = gate off (write the voice's waveform byte with bit 0 clear to $D404/$D40B/$D412), 1-94 = set the frequency from music_freq_lo/hi ($C374/$C3D3,note) and retrigger (JSR $C324/$C335/$C346). A voice the mode silences is gated off every step. Afterwards, with music_keys_enabled ($C439) set, JSR $CB51 (an editor hook whose code is gone: $CB51 is now note data of block 1); then JMP ($CB05) to the KERNAL IRQ. A note therefore lasts until the next non-zero byte in its column; a gate-off lets the release run.
Music: move to the next block of the pattern: music_block ($C435) + 1, music_step ($C436) = 1, JMP $C1B2 to recompute the block pointer and play step 1.
Music: SEI, JSR music_save_irq ($CB14: saves $0314/$0315 in $CB05/$CB06 and installs music_first_irq $C2EB), 7 NOPs, CLI, RTS. The tail of music_init ($C09B).
Six NOPs ($EA) after music_hook_irq's RTS: never executed, padding.

Music: the first IRQ after music_init (installed in $0314 by $CB14). Loads music_tick_count ($C438) with the step length (music_tempo $C443) of the song's first pattern (music_order_first entry 1, $CAC4); zeroes the CIA 1 time-of-day clock (writes 0 to $DC0B, $DC0A, $DC09, $DC08; nothing in the image reads the clock back, byte search for $DC08-$DC0B); music_position ($C433) = 1; installs music_irq ($C0AF) in $0314/$0315; JMP $C183 to start position 1, which plays its first step and chains to the KERNAL IRQ.
Five NOPs ($EA) after music_first_irq's JMP $C183: never executed, padding.
Music: $C43B = 0 and A = music_block ($C435): the start of the x64 multiply in music_block_pointer ($C1B2).
Music: retrigger voice 1: X = music_pattern ($C434); writes music_v1_ctrl ($C483,X) to $D404 with the gate bit clear, then with it set, so the envelope starts again on every note.
Music: retrigger voice 2: waveform byte music_v2_ctrl ($C4C3,pattern) to $D40B, gate off then gate on.
Music: retrigger voice 3: waveform byte music_v3_ctrl ($C503,pattern) to $D412, gate off then gate on.
Music: before each step: if music_keys_enabled ($C439) is set, load the KERNAL's last key $C5 and go to music_key_voice_select ($C1CF); otherwise straight on to $C1F9 -> $C364.
Music: music_voice_mode ($C437) = 4 means stop: JMP music_song_end ($C103). Otherwise reload it and JMP music_play_step ($C1FC).

Music: SID frequency table, low bytes, indexed by note number 0-94 ($C374-$C3D2); the high bytes are music_freq_hi ($C3D3). Index 0 is $00FF, not a note (a note byte 0 means hold). Note n is the semitone n above C0 counted as 12 x octave + pitch (12 = C1, 48 = C4, 57 = A4 = $1CD6, 94 = A#7 = $F467); at the PAL clock (985,248 Hz) every entry is about a quarter semitone flat of equal temperament (A4 = 433.5 Hz). Read by $C22B, $C26C, $C2B0.
Music: SID frequency table, high bytes for notes 0-94 ($C3D3-$C431), pairs with music_freq_lo ($C374). Read by $C231, $C272, $C2B6.
One byte $EA after the frequency tables; not read by the player (no reference found).
Music variable: the song's order position, 1 to music_song_len ($C43D); set to 1 by $C304, advanced by $C0F5; indexes music_order_first/last ($CAC3/$CADB). 1 at the hand-over.

Music variable: the pattern playing (1-63 possible), from music_order_first ($C189), advanced at $C0E4; indexes every per-pattern table $C443-$CA83. 1 at the hand-over, 2 in the play snapshot (the tune was stopped in its second pattern when play took the IRQ).
Music variable: the note block playing, from music_block_first ($C1A9), advanced by $C2CD; compared with music_block_last at $C0C6; the block's data is at $CAF2 + 64 x block (pointer in $C43A/$C43B).
Music variable: the step (row) within the block, 1-16; set from music_first_step ($C1AF) or 1 ($C2D2), advanced at $C0C0 every music_tempo ticks; the Y index of the note reads in music_play_step.
Music variable: which voices play: 0 all (the game's setting, $C09D), 1-3 that voice alone, 4 stop. Changed only by music_key_voice_select ($C1F5), which runs only when music_keys_enabled is set.
Music variable: IRQs left in this step; decremented by music_irq ($C0AF), reloaded from music_tempo ($C0BD, $C0A9, $C2F1).

Music variable: non-zero turns on the music editor's keyboard controls ($C357) and its per-step hook JSR $CB51 ($C2C2). Only ever written with 0 (music_init $C0A0); byte search for $C439 finds no other writer. 0 at the hand-over.

Music variable, two bytes $C43A/$C43B: address of the current note block, $CAF2 + 64 x music_block, written by $C1C1/$C1C9 ($C43B also used as the shift register at $C1B8); copied +$10/+$20/+$30 to $FB/$FC for each voice's column. $CB32 at the hand-over (block 1).
Music variable: high byte of music_block_ptr ($C43A); zeroed by $C31D, used as the shift register of the x64 multiply at $C1B8, then $CA added at $C1C7.
Music constant: steps in a full block, $10 (16); compared at $C0D9. Only this reader found.
Music constant: the number of order positions the song plays, 1; compared at $C0FB. So only order entry 1 (patterns 1-2) plays; entries 2-6 of the order tables are never reached.
Five bytes $C43E-$C442 (00 00 B3 CD 04) after the music variables; no reader or writer found by byte search. Unknown, perhaps editor state.

Music, per-pattern table (64 bytes, index = music_pattern; the title tune uses entries 1 and 2; entries 3-63 hold values for patterns the song never reaches (3-13 are named by the unused order entries), and entry 0 is unused): IRQ ticks per step; pattern 1 and 2: 8. Read at $C0A6, $C0BA, $C2EE.
